title: MCP Architecture and Transports
description: Understand MCP hosts, clients, servers, transports, and how they fit into existing .NET architectures.

blocks.text: MCP has three logical participants: a host, a client, and a server. The host owns the AI session, the client connects to the server on behalf of the host, and the server exposes tools, resources, and prompts. Transports determine how the client and server communicate.

blocks.title: Responsibility map
items: **Host** — orchestrates the AI session and decides which servers to connect.
**Client** — speaks MCP on behalf of the host; discovers tools and invokes them.
**Server** — implements business logic and exposes it through MCP primitives.

blocks.title: Stdio transport configuration
blocks.content: Configure an MCP server to communicate over stdin/stdout for local IDE integration.

cards.title: stdio
cards.description: Standard input/output transport for local child processes.

cards.title: HTTP + SSE
cards.description: Remote transport using HTTP for requests and server-sent events for responses.

cards.title: Streamable HTTP
cards.description: A newer transport style that supports bidirectional communication over HTTP.
pros: Simpler than separate HTTP and SSE endpoints

blocks.title: Start with stdio locally
blocks.text: For local development and IDE plugins, stdio is the simplest path. Move to HTTP transports once you need remote access or want to expose the server to multiple clients.

items.hint: stdio for local processes, HTTP for remote services

items.text: I understand where MCP fits in an existing backend
items.hint: As an AI-aware interface layer wrapping current APIs and data access

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: MCP cleanly separates the host, client, and server responsibilities.
stdio is easiest for local development; HTTP/SSE is better for remote services.
C# backends can host MCP servers without replacing existing APIs.
blocks.takeaway: Choose your transport based on deployment topology. For learning, stdio is faster; for production, HTTP/SSE is more flexible.
